drhp.business: The Company manufactures and supplies power and control cables, having widened its portfolio over three decades to include aerial bunched cables, instrumentation cables, building wires and conductors. It serves state electricity boards, EPC contractors, public sector undertakings, and customers in oil & gas, mining, steel, real estate and electrical panel manufacturing across a pan-India footprint.

risks.note: Key raw materials copper and aluminium are commodities subject to price volatility linked to global metal markets, which can impact input costs, margins and working capital if not passed through or hedged.

Business is working-capital intensive given institutional/government-oriented sales; debtor days increased from 65 in FY25 to 85 in FY26, and cash conversion cycle stood at 81 days in FY26 (73 in FY25), reflecting extended collection cycles.
risks.risk: Working capital intensity and elongating receivables

risks.note: Top 10 clients accounted for approximately 55% of revenue; government and EPC-billed-on-behalf-of-government clients accounted for 50.9% of revenue in FY26 (down from 74.5% in FY25), indicating continuing dependence on a limited set of large institutional/government customers.

The Indian cables and wires industry is highly fragmented with over 100 domestic manufacturers and multiple regional/mid-sized players, which could exert pricing pressure in less differentiated product categories.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity in a fragmented industry

risks.note: Participation in institutional and government tenders is contingent on maintaining BIS, ISO and NABL certifications and complying with bid-qualification and vendor-approval conditions across states; any lapse could affect tender eligibility and revenue visibility.

Growth plans depend on timely commissioning and ramp-up of the new Ghiloth (Unit-III) MV cable facility and achieving targeted utilisation (28% FY27, 45% FY28, ramping to 85% at peak); delays, cost overruns or slower demand ramp-up could affect the growth trajectory.

Despite improved net debt-to-equity (0.6x in FY26 from 2.5x in FY25), continued capacity expansion including the ₹39.9 crore new manufacturing unit exposes the Company to interest rate and refinancing risk.

- licence/regulatory: multi-state vendor/tender eligibility built over time — evidence: cumulative state vendor approvals reached 20 states in FY26 after 5 additional states were added during the year
- distribution: broad institutional client base …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Key raw materials copper and aluminium are commodities subject to price volatility linked to global metal markets, which can impact input costs, margins and working capital if not passed through or hedged.
- Business is working-capital intensive given institutional/government-oriented sales; debtor days increased from 65 in FY25 to 85 in FY26, and cash conversion cycle stood at 81 days in FY26 (73 in FY25), reflecting extended collection cycles.
- Top 10 clients accounted for approximately 55% of revenue; government and EPC-billed-on-behalf-of-government clients accounted for 50.9% of revenue in FY26 (down from 74.5% in FY25), indicating continuing dependence on a limited set of large institutional/government customers.
- The Indian cables and wires industry is highly fragmented with over 100 domestic manufacturers and multiple regional/mid-sized players, which could exert pricing pressure in less differentiated product categories.
- Participation in institutional and government tenders is contingent on maintaining BIS, ISO and NABL certifications and complying with bid-qualification and vendor-approval conditions across states; any lapse could affect tender eligibility and revenue visibility.
- Growth plans depend on timely commissioning and ramp-up of the new Ghiloth (Unit-III) MV cable facility and achieving targeted utilisation (28% FY27, 45% FY28, ramping to 85% at peak); delays, cost overruns or slower demand ramp-up could affect the growth trajectory.
- Despite improved net debt-to-equity (0.6x in FY26 from 2.5x in FY25), continued capacity expansion including the ₹39.9 crore new manufacturing unit exposes the Company to interest rate and refinancing risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Entry into the medium voltage (MV) cable segment via the new Ghiloth Unit-III facility, extending the product portfolio into a higher-value category.
- Deepening wallet share with existing institutional clients (electricity boards, EPC players, PSUs) by cross-selling higher-value, higher-margin products including MV cables.
- Expanding geographical footprint into underpenetrated and new states, leveraging existing multi-state vendor approvals.
- Diversifying customer mix by increasing the share of private-sector customers, reducing dependence on government/PSU-oriented business.
